summary: SL-105 added a test-only guard for the file-row half of SL-063's Revised latch. The guard is one real-tree Fact, TopLevelTests.AnInPlaceCorrectionOfARootLevelFileNameMarksThatFileRowRevised (TopLevelTests.cs:121-147), with no src change. It hardlinks root\a-stale.bin to sub\current.bin, grows the file by 63 MiB through the sub name, and scans with Watch(correctedRows: ["a-stale.bin"]). The Fact was effectively finished in the build-check and risk-spike candidates before design began. Most of the slice's cost and every post-build finding came from the mutant-kill tooling the critique asked for: Mutants.ps1, a leaked-copy sweep (ScratchRoots.ps1), and an 11-row corpus with its runner. Of the 3 code-review findings and 3 critique findings, all 3 code-review findings were in that tooling, none in the Fact. All three were then waived to the backlog (SC-326, SC-327, SC-328), plus O-009 to SC-330.

payload.estimate_error: Opened medium size, medium risk, 1 designer. Risk was over-tiered. The slice is test-only with no src change. The final Fact was already written and passing in the build-check and spike temp copies. It was stable in every run recorded: 63 spike executions (30 + 30 isolated, 3 full-suite runs), 15 isolated validate runs on the host, and 10 in a fresh Windows 11 Sandbox. File count was under-estimated. The design said about 30 lines in TopLevelTests.cs plus the two repro files. The build added four more files under tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard: Mutants.ps1, ScratchRoots.ps1, ScratchRootCorpus.json and ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1. The Fact itself is +39 lines (validate: git diff --stat 1d271a0..HEAD). Medium effort held, but only because critique findings M1 and m1 added a tooling sub-project. For a bare "add one Fact" the real size was small.

learned.lesson: On a test-only 'guard the mutant' slice, size the mutant-kill proof, not the Fact. The critique will require the kill check to be a committed runnable script (CC-004) that sweeps leaked copies (CC-009). On SL-105 that turned a roughly 40-line Fact into the Fact plus Mutants.ps1, ScratchRoots.ps1, a corpus JSON and a corpus runner. Hand the designer CC-004 and CC-009 up front and count the tooling in the file estimate.
learned.evidence: Design: 'about 30 lines in one existing file plus the two repro files'. Build changed list adds 4 more files under tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard. Findings: 3 of 3 code-review findings (SC-301 copy, ping orphan, order check) were in those scripts; 0 in TopLevelTests.cs.

learned.lesson: 'Model it on SL-102's Mutants.ps1' copies SL-102's open defects. The critique's own M1 fix text prescribed ending with `git diff --exit-code -- src`, which is the SC-301 defect (fails when src was dirty before the run). When a design or critique says 'modelled on X', the same gate should check the defects already filed against X. Mutants.ps1 now exists as two diverging copies (Get-SrcDigest, Set-Sdk, Read-Trx and Invoke-Dn are duplicated), and SC-301 lives in both.
learned.evidence: Code-review finding m1 (Mutants.ps1:237-238, copied from SL-102 Mutants.ps1:250-252). Build 'drift' note about the duplicated helpers. SC-326 is the carried item.

learned.lesson: Do not assume an 'accepted-pending' minor finding in a committed script gets fixed in-slice on this loop. All three code-review findings were accepted-pending, and all three ended as waived obligations carried to the backlog. The m1 disposition even said 'so this is not deferred' and then O-013 was waived as 'a miss nobody required'. Planning should treat accepted minors in tests/bugs scripts as backlog, or the disposition text should say so.
learned.evidence: O-013 -> SC-326, O-014 -> SC-327, O-015 -> SC-328, each 'waived'. Validate re-observed the ping.exe orphan and recorded a failed check ('The corpus runner leaves no process running after it returns') for a one-line fix (start PING.EXE directly).

learned.lesson: For a missing-test bug where build-check has already run a candidate Fact against the mutant, the risk spike's mutant experiment repeats it. Spike 1 re-measured build-check's result (candidate Fact passes on baseline; mutant A fails only that Fact, same 'snapshot 4, row a-stale.bin: Revised is False' message). Only spike 2 (stability) added information. Aim the spike at what build-check did not measure: flakiness in the parallel suite, other environments, the Windows-folder path.
learned.evidence: Build-check commands: 'Failed 1/25 ... only the candidate Fact' and spike 1: 'Failed 1/25 ... snapshot 4, row a-stale.bin: Revised is False, its figures moved in snapshot 1'. Design's Fact body is spike 1's diff verbatim.

learned.lesson: TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot (TempTree.cs:62-76) redirects any TEMP at or under the Windows folder to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests, so Core.Tests TempTree fixtures never land under C:\Windows\Temp. A 'run with TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP' arm varies only the process temp (vstest, trx), not where the fixture lives. Do not carry it as an owed case for TempTree-based Facts. SL-105 did, and Mutants.ps1 got -Temp Engine/Ordinary arms that double its runs (42 s build, 50 s validate against the engine case runner's 120 s limit, Q-222).
learned.evidence: Spike 2: tree.Root printed C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-tests\<guid> in all 63 runs, in both TEMP arms. Design case 'run under the engine's temp folder' (C-006) kept anyway.

learned.lesson: A fixture built on a stale directory-entry cache must assert the stale precondition from the first snapshot BEFORE any probe-derived counter. Scanner.cs:504-524 increments _probes before the size comparison and sets ProbeCorrected only when the sizes differ. A refreshed entry therefore passes 'Probes == 1' and fails at the flags assert, which reads like a product regression rather than a spoiled fixture. In the Fact, the snapshot-0 assert (TopLevelTests.cs:136) now comes right after Completed.
learned.evidence: Critique m2 (confirmed against Scanner.cs:504-524). Build O-012: with Append before Hardlink the Fact fails at :136 with Expected (File, Done, 1048576, False) / Actual (File, Done, 67108864, False).

learned.lesson: There is no real tree on this PC that produces a stale root-level File row, so the file-row Revised path can only be exercised with a fabricated fixture. C:\Windows root has 37 files, 14 with link count above 1, and 0 whose directory-entry size differs from the by-name size. C:\ProgramData's real corrections (#244) reach folder rows. Do not plan a 'real drive, shipped exe' validation for this latch. The unreached item in SL-105's validate cannot be satisfied by scanning anything that exists today.
learned.evidence: Investigation: '0 of 37 had a directory-entry size different from the by-name size'. Build-check re-measure: 37 files, 14 multi-name (GetFileInformationByHandle). Validate 'not reached: a real stale hardlink on a real drive'.

learned.lesson: An imported 'must-verify' precondition whose only discharge is a machine the project does not have (Windows 10) halts validate once and then gets waived. Windows 10 is already open as Q-192/Q-224 and was carried to SC-330. Record such a precondition at design as waived/carried, not as an obligation aimed at validate.
learned.evidence: validate-slice #1 halted: 'the validation passed, but 1 obligation (O-009) aimed at this stage is still open'. Design lists it must-verify and says 'already open under Q-192/Q-224 and not raised again'. validate #2 passed after O-009 was waived.

learned.lesson: Windows Sandbox runs of Core.Tests TempTree Facts are valid only as an ordinary medium-integrity local user. SYSTEM's temp is forced to C:\Windows\SystemTemp and TempTree refuses to build there. Run as a local user via schtasks /ru <user> /rl LIMITED, set TEMP/TMP to a user-writable folder, and use the single-Fact filter. The TopLevel filter reads 23/25 in the Sandbox because Developer Mode is off there and the 2 symlink tests fail with error 1314 (Q-001). That is not a regression.
learned.evidence: Validate: Sandbox run 1 as SYSTEM invalid; run 2 as local user 'fsa': Fact 10/10, TopLevel filter 23/25 with the 2 symlink failures.

learned.lesson: A coverage-gap repro on this project is a source-text reader. Here FileRowRevisedGuardTests.cs uses 5 regexes over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests, so a green repro proves the words, not the behaviour. The mutant kill is what ties the Fact to the defect. The design must be checked regex by regex against the planned test text, and the Revised assert must stay a literal-true tuple inside the Fact's own unit. The SL-102 precedent is the same shape.
learned.evidence: Design selection_rationale (3) and contract error_cases. O-002 and O-006 discharged separately: repro 1/1 and Mutants.ps1 'exactly the new Fact red under mutant A'.

what_went_wrong: Five stages ran twice (build-check, design-slice, critique, code-review, validate-slice) and none of the second runs changed the Fact. The reasons were: design #1 hit a provider session limit; build-check #1 read its own 'Nothing of this slice exists yet' wording as 'partial'; critique #1 and code-review #1 waited on dispositions; validate #1 halted on the unsatisfiable O-009. The reruns overstate how hard the slice was, but they cost real gate time.

The design's file count was wrong in the way lesson #388 warns about. It cited #388 and checked only that no test pins TopLevelTests' method names. The undercount came from the critique's M1 and m1 remedies instead (3 files promised, 7 delivered).

Mutants.ps1 shipped with a known defect. The critique's M1 fix text prescribed the `git diff --exit-code -- src` closing check (SC-301). Code review found it, and the disposition said 'not deferred'. O-013 was then waived to SC-326. The committed guard still exits 1 whenever src was already dirty, which is exactly the case it is run for (uncommitted TopLevel*.cs work).

The ping.exe orphan (R2-m2) was waived to SC-327 as minor, although the fix is one line. Validate then re-observed it and recorded a failed check, and every later run of ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1 leaves a ping.exe behind. The R2-m3 ordering check is still unguarded (SC-328): the corpus can say 'before anything was removed' while checking only a count.
Validate #1 halted solely on O-009 (Windows 10). The design had already said this was open under Q-192/Q-224. It still became an obligation that no stage could discharge.

Spike 1 repeated build-check's mutant measurement. The design stage then restated spike 1's diff as its single proposal. The test-only slice paid for the same experiment in three stages (build-check, spike 1, build).

The 'engine TEMP' case (C-006) survived into the design and into Mutants.ps1's -Temp Engine/Ordinary arms even though spike 2 had shown it is location-neutral (ChooseTestsRoot redirects the fixture). It roughly doubled the script's runtime for no extra coverage.

All six critique and code-review dispositions (3 + 3) were answered by a model and none was triaged by a person (Q-251 already open). The first Sandbox validation run, as SYSTEM, was invalid and had to be redone.

missed.what: The critique's M1 fix told the builder to end the committed Mutants.ps1 with 'a src hash plus `git diff --exit-code -- src`'. That is SL-102's SC-301 defect: the check returns 1 whenever src was dirty before the run, even though the script's own digest exists for that case. The critique did not ask what the closing check does when src has uncommitted edits, and it did not check the open defects on the script it told the builder to model on.
missed.caught_by: code-review (finding m1, Mutants.ps1:237-238); then waived to SC-326

missed.what: The design imported 'NTFS per-name staleness holds on Windows 10' as status must-verify. The critique did not ask which stage could discharge it when no Windows 10 machine exists and Q-192/Q-224 already record that. It became O-009, which halted validate once and was waived to SC-330.

The first-pass code review accepted ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1 starting its live non-PowerShell process as `cmd /c ping -n 120 127.0.0.1` and stopping only cmd.exe. ping.exe outlives the run by up to about 120 s, which contradicts the header's 'stops what it started'. A first-pass check of the script's cleanup path (kill what you start) would have found it.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (R2-m2), re-observed by validate; waived to SC-327

missed.what: The first-pass review passed the corpus check labelled 'the build servers were shut down once, before anything was removed'. That check asserts only `$State.Released -eq 1`. Moving `& $Release` after the removal loop in ScratchRoots.ps1 still exits 0 with all 11 rows held, so the ordering that m1 asked for is guarded by nothing. A mutation of the new corpus's own checks would have shown it.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (R2-m3, by mutating a temp copy); waived to SC-328

lessons_judged.why: The design ran its 'one Fact undercounts' coherence check (grep for pins on TopLevelTests names, nameof, pinned arrays) and found none. The undercount still happened, from a source the lesson does not name: critique-demanded mutant tooling took the file count from 3 to 7.
The Fact never touches a-stale.bin by name between Append and Watch, and it asserts the stale 1 MiB at snapshot 0 (TopLevelTests.cs:136). Spike 2 saw snapshot 0 at 1,048,576 in 63 of 63 runs.

It restates the stale-hardlink-name mechanism, but the investigation had already measured it on this machine. The lesson's rule about reading sizes through the probe rules did not bear on a test-only slice.

It concerns folder-row corrections under C:\ProgramData. This slice's target is a root-level File row, which has no real source on this PC (C:\Windows root: 14 of 37 multi-name files, 0 stale), so the ProgramData advice does not help the unreached real-drive check.
The Fact reuses TempTree.Hardlink (cmd.exe mklink /H) and TempTree.Append unelevated, and builds no native helper. Spikes 1 and 2 ran it unelevated.
Every command went through eng/dotnet.ps1. The critique's m1 reused the worktree's .dotnet through DOTNET_ROOT/PATH in Mutants.ps1 instead of bootstrapping about 300 MB of SDK into each scratch copy.

unknowns: Is tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard registered as a bug-catalog row and re-run at every later validate? The design's claim is recalled from Q-249 and Q-250 and never checked against the running engine. If it is not registered, the repro guards nothing after merge, and only the Fact in the default suite remains. Neither Mutants.ps1 nor the corpus runner is run by anything routine.

Does NTFS per-name hardlink staleness hold on Windows 10 (SC-330, Q-192/Q-224)? If it does not, the Fact goes red at TopLevelTests.cs:136 on a Windows 10 machine and cannot be skipped, because CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped covers it. The Fact is measured only on Windows 11 builds 26200 and 26100.9457.

Does Defender at defaults open the stale name between the Append and the scan on a machine where it is running? On the host the Fact never saw it (63 spike, 15 validate and 10 Sandbox runs). Validate did not read Defender's state on the host, and Defender was not running in the Sandbox.

Mutant C (Seed builds the row before Settle) is killed by 2 existing TopLevel tests, but the investigation never captured their failure messages. It is unknown whether they die for the right reason (the watcher's 'Revised in the snapshot it settled in' assertion) or by accident. This matters before any standing TopLevelTracker mutant roster is built.
